Regarding $NBIS earnings results:

To show you how fast they're growing... from Q2 to Q3: 

Revenue: $582.3M -> $980.8M (+68% QoQ)
Adjusted EBITDA: $236.2M -> $465.8M (+97% QoQ)
AI cloud adj. EBITDA margin: 49.7% -> 53.2%
Net Income: −$190.4M -> −$37.5M

ARR has reached $6.4B at the end of Sep. In terms of management commentary: 

- Since start of Q3, Nebius signed $12B+ of new contracts
- Average GPU pricing rose 20%+ sequentially, payback shortened from 22M -> 19M
- On Q3 deals, prepayments covered 100% of associated capex, up from 50–60% in Q2 (insane for financing)
- Contract value per MW exceeded $25M+ from Q3 up from ~$20M Q2 
- 5GW contracted power year end

With $10B of committed customer prepayments in 2026 and $17B-$20B in 2027. Now, prepayments and borrowing against existing contracts covers ~75-85% of 2027 capex. 

On subsidiaries:
1. Avride - 250 autonomous vehicles fleet, over 100,000 passenger rides (with companies like $UBER). Fully driverless robotaxi targeted H1 2027.
2. Toloka - Revenue doubled sequentially
3. Enterprise cloud - Databricks and Datadog selected Neibus. Along with a new agreement with Snowflake. 
4. Tavily - Over 3M developers now with $IBM post-training a core partner. 
5. ClickHouse - Nothing about new secondary valuations, but we can see valuations growing
6. TokenFactory - Contract value grew 17x sequentially

The primary negative I saw was that 2026 guidance is now on the lower end (near ~$3B), due to $MSFT capacity deliveries slipping to Q2 2027.

Apparently there was an execution miss with a third party partner DataOne. Temporary generators were retired amid permitting issues before enough $BE fuel cell capacity came online. 

Capex also increased in 2026 from $20B-$25B to $27B, while revising revenue expectations downward. 

So near-term unfortunate headwinds kinda reminiscent of AOI earnings; however long term I think Nebius will take care of you. 

For 2027 outlook:
- $12-13 billion revenue, capex of $40-45 billion, pre-tax breakeven by the end of 2027.

Very operationally bullish, as seen with prepayments covering capex, GPU premiums increasing. Main downside is near-term execution risk from third parties, causing near-term delays and revenue recognition. 

Great quarter from Nebius overall.

Taking a step back from the Jensen news.

This hits at a moment of broader AI anxiety: multi-year buildout costs, geopolitical delays on data centers, and the risk that new models reduce the need for expensive inference. All of it has fed the selloff.

None of it changes the underlying reality. We’re still early. Adoption is sub 1%, and the steep part of the inference S-curve is still ahead of us. 

Nvidia’s GPUs remain a step-function better than AMD’s, evidenced by ~
90% GPU market share even at a higher price.

The uncertainty in $NVDA creates a window for new capital to come in and benefit from the next several years of the AI buildout, of which Nvidia will account for about 50% of that cost.

Jensen Huang’s resignation ends an era at NVIDIA and forces a stress test on the AI trade.

Huang wasn’t just a CEO. He was the face, the product visionary and the operator who turned NVIDIA into the $4T+ foundation of the AI boom. Key-man risk was always priced in at some level; today it is no longer theoretical. $NVDA stock is already down hard (10%+ in premarket) and the rest of the AI complex is feeling the spillover.

The near-term picture is messy. Leadership uncertainty, succession questions and the China-related overhang from the scandal create real noise. Colette Kress (long-time CFO, now interim CEO) and the existing leadership team provide operational continuity and the board has appointed Harvey Jones as its first Chair. Product roadmaps, CUDA lock-in and hyperscaler demand don’t disappear overnight. Still, the narrative premium from $NVDA is gone.

The setup for a multi-week rally is strong. AI stocks were already deeply oversold coming into this news after the recent sharp selloff. Technicals are washed out, sentiment is depressed and multiple strategists had already called the prior dip extreme. Forced selling and panic often exhaust quickly in these regimes. A relief bounce across the AI complex over the next several weeks looks highly probable as the dust settles.

The multi-month view is more nuanced. The AI infrastructure buildout itself is not over. Capex remains massive, data-centre demand is still the dominant growth driver and the underlying technology stack (accelerated computing, inference, networking) continues to expand. What changes is that NVIDIA must now prove it can execute without its founder-CEO narrative. Succession clarity, any regulatory/export fallout and whether the next permanent CEO can maintain the same cultural and technical intensity will decide if this is a healthy reset or the start of a longer period of relative underperformance versus the broader AI complex.

This is a classic “sell the rumor / buy the fact” environment for the trade. Oversold conditions favour a multi-week bounce. The multi-month case for AI stocks rests on whether the structural demand story can remain intact and companies with high margins, FCF and strong balance-sheets are likely to outperform. https://t.co/YKr5pL7G2c

The world is not ready for a swarm of agents. Everything will explode from infra (CI, Git, API) to the token consumption.

Today most people still work with one agent, one prompt at a time. But that agent can already spawn subagents, move to the cloud and run for hours, and stay on in the background 24/7. 

The next step is one agent starting a thousand others, and then swarms that never stop. Each step multiplies token consumption, and by the end we are talking about something like 10,000x what a single agent burns today. 

IMO nothing we built was sized for this. Git was designed for humans pushing a few times a day, CI for a handful of builds, APIs for a human rate of requests. A swarm breaks all of it at once. We need a new infrastructure, built for swarms of agents.

Some quick observations on Anthropic's IPO:

1/ The number of customers paying $100K or more grew 12x in a year, to over 11,900. And the existing ones are spending about 9x what they did 1 year ago (wild).

2/ The net loss is $23.3B, but $21.9B of that is a paper loss. They owe early investors shares, and those shares got more valuable, so accounting rules count it as a loss (has to do with convertible notes etc being exchanged)

3/ Revenue per employee is over $6.6M!

4/ They did $17B in revenue last quarter, and that's up more than 12x from a year ago.

5/ The stat they feature most is compute efficiency, where they say they get 4x more revenue per dollar of compute than in early 2025. ( I think this is a metric they defined themselves but not 100% sure)

6/ It's a public benefit corporation, so shareholders are buying into a company that's legally allowed to weigh other goals alongside their returns.

7/ You can request shares at the IPO price through Robinhood, SoFi, Schwab, Fidelity and E*TRADE, which I think is somewhat unusual for an IPO this size, but maybe it's a sign of the times?

8/ The whole roadshow is an 11 chapter video that anyone can watch, and it's cool that they shared it.

9/ The ticker is $ANT. It's expected to price on November 18 and start trading the next day.

10/ One of the case studies is about Sparky, Walmart’s shopping assistant, and they say orders through it are about 35% bigger. What’s interesting to me is that shoppers only ever see Walmart, and Anthropic is the plumbing underneath. Sidenote: I co-founded @MeetLCA an agency that builds experiences like this big companies/big startups so this trend is what I'm seeing too (demand for agent experience products)

11/ The founders' letter tells investors to "never let your company be worth a dollar more than it is actually worth." I haven't seen that in an IPO pitch before.

12/ About 250 customers pay them $10M or more a year, and over 1,900 pay $1M or more.

13/ They spent $9.9B on compute last quarter, which is more than half of revenue. $5B of that was bought on short-term deals that cost a lot more, which tells me demand is running ahead of what they planned for.

14/ All 7 co-founders are still at the company, and they lose about 1% of the people they want to keep each year.

15/ They recorded $1.1B in stock based compensation last quarter.

16/ They have about $96B in cash and have raised about $141B in total.

Note: this is not financial advice. Do your own research. I share things I find interesting about startups and building businesses in real-time.

Whether you're into AI or not, this is a historic moment for tech, AI and the USA.
